headline: Compaq passes IBM as the biggest PC maker
text: Compaq, which began by copying the IBM PC, sold more personal computers than IBM or Apple in 1994; in the US it had 12.6% of the market against Apple's 11.6%. In 1991 a price war had brought Compaq its first loss and its first layoffs.

headline: Kobe earthquake, then Barings collapses on Nikkei bets
text: An earthquake struck Kobe on 17 January, killing more than 5,000 people and wrecking the port; the Nikkei fell 1,025 points the next day. On 26 February Barings, Britain's oldest merchant bank, collapsed after its Singapore trader Nick Leeson lost hundreds of millions of pounds betting on Nikkei futures.
imageCaption: A collapsed section of elevated highway in Kobe after the earthquake, 17 January 1995

headline: McDonald's: 26 billion dollars of sales in 79 countries
text: Systemwide sales reached nearly 26 billion dollars in 1994 and net income passed 1.2 billion. McDonald's had 15,205 restaurants at the end of the year in 79 countries, up from 70 a year earlier; 5,461 restaurants are now outside the United States, and sales abroad are growing much faster than at home. The shares were split two-for-one in June 1994.
source: https://archive.org/download/mcdonaldscorpannualreports/mcdonalds1994_djvu.txt (1994 annual report, 11-year summary, read 2026-10-03); yearly change from data/out/mcd.json

headline: The dollar collapses, the franc soars
text: The dollar fell to new lows in March: on 31 March it was traded at about 1.17 francs in New York, almost 13% less than at the end of 1994. The swings drove the Zurich exchange; the Swiss National Bank and the Bundesbank lowered interest rates during the last week of March. Swiss shares are down for the year in francs, and bank shares were also weighed down by currency-trading worries.
source: Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 1 April 1995, p. 33 ('Neuer schwerer Schwächeanfall des Dollars'; 'Die Zürcher Börse vom 27. bis zum 31. März: Diktat des Dollars an den Aktienringen'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1995-04-01.pdf (read 2026-10-03); data/raw/fred/DEXSZUS.csv (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Markus Lusser, chairman of the Swiss National Bank
imageCredit: Regina Kühne (Universität St. Gallen, HSG Archiv)

headline: The dollar falls below 80 yen
text: In April the dollar fell below 80 yen for the first time, from about 99 at the end of January. The strong yen is crushing Japan's exporters in an economy that is barely growing.
imageCaption: A Tokyo foreign-exchange dealing room as the dollar hits a record low of 80.15 yen, 10 April 1995
imageCredit: Photo by KAZUHIRO NOGI/AFP via Getty Images

headline: LDDS becomes WorldCom and buys WilTel's network
text: At its annual meeting LDDS renamed itself WorldCom. It is buying WilTel Network Services of Tulsa, Oklahoma, a long-distance network operator, for $2.5 billion in cash. WorldCom lost nearly $150 million in 1994 because of the IDB merger, on revenue that doubled to $2.2 billion.

headline: Bankverein buys S.G. Warburg
text: The Bankverein is buying S.G. Warburg, the leading London merchant bank, for about £860 million ($1.34 billion), after earlier buying the Chicago options trader O'Connor & Associates and the Chicago asset manager Brinson Partners. Combined with its own investment bank, the business will be called SBC Warburg.
imageCaption: Georges Blum, head of the Schweizerischer Bankverein, at the St. Gallen management symposium, 1994
imageCredit: Regina Kühne (Universität St. Gallen, HSG Archiv)

headline: The 777 enters service
text: United Airlines put the Boeing 777 into passenger service in June. It is the first airliner designed entirely on computers and the first approved for long flights over water on two engines from the day it entered service.
imageCaption: A United Airlines Boeing 777, the type's first customer, taxiing at Frankfurt in June 1995, the month it entered service

headline: Windows 95 launches with a billion-dollar campaign
text: Microsoft launched Windows 95 on 24 August, with the Rolling Stones' Start Me Up in its advertising and a marketing effort estimated at a billion dollars. One million copies shipped worldwide in the first four days. It has a Start button and a taskbar, and runs on Intel chips.
imageCaption: Bill Gates and Jay Leno on stage at the Windows 95 launch, Microsoft's campus in Redmond, 24 August 1995

headline: Netscape's IPO: 2.9 billion dollars for a company without profits
text: Netscape, the maker of the most popular web browser, went public on 9 August. The price was doubled at the last minute to 28 dollars; the shares opened at 71, touched 75 and closed at 58.25, valuing the 16-month-old company at 2.9 billion dollars.
imageCaption: Netscape's founders Jim Clark and Marc Andreessen, the 24-year-old who wrote the first popular web browser, mid-1990s

headline: Japan's bank failures spread; Daiwa loses $1.1 billion in New York
text: In July Cosmo Credit Cooperative in Tokyo failed, and in August Kizu Credit Cooperative, whose losses are expected to exceed 1 trillion yen, and Hyogo Bank in western Japan followed. In September Daiwa Bank, one of the big city banks, said a trader at its New York branch had lost about $1.1 billion through fraud. A Finance Ministry inspection this summer put the losses of the seven jusen, housing loan companies set up by banks that lent heavily to property developers in the 1980s, at 6.4 trillion yen. Five years after the crash, the bubble's bad loans are coming to the surface.

headline: PlayStation launches in America and Europe
text: The PlayStation went on sale in North America on 9 September and in Europe on 29 September.
imageCaption: The original Sony PlayStation with its controller

headline: Yitzhak Rabin assassinated at a peace rally
text: Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was shot dead on 4 November in Tel Aviv as he left a rally for the peace process attended by more than 100,000 people. The killer, Yigal Amir, is a 25-year-old Israeli law student opposed to the Oslo Accords. Shimon Peres has taken over.
imageCaption: Yitzhak Rabin speaks at the peace rally in Tel Aviv, 4 November 1995
imageCredit: Israel Press and Photo Agency (I.P.P.A.) photographer

headline: Toy Story, the first film made entirely by computer
text: Toy Story, made by Steve Jobs's Pixar and released by Disney, opened in American cinemas on 22 November and set a record for its opening weekend. It is the first feature film made entirely by computer animation. Tom Hanks and Tim Allen voice a cowboy doll and a space ranger toy.

headline: Nokia warns on profits; shares plunge
text: After four years of very fast growth, Nokia's mobile phone business has hit trouble: delayed chip deliveries halted some assembly lines, inventories are building, and North American carriers are switching to digital more slowly than Nokia expected. On 14 December Nokia warned that profits may suffer. Its share price fell 28% within five days.

headline: Switzerland's first internet café opens in Zurich
text: On Friday 15 December the first internet café in Switzerland opened at Uraniastrasse 3 in Zurich: coffee, pizza and ten computers connected to the internet. Hardly anybody has the internet at home yet, so for many visitors it is the first time they see a web page; the café also gives courses for beginners. Such cafés are appearing in cities all over the world: Helsinki had one in 1993, London's Cyberia opened in September 1994, and three opened in New York's East Village this June.
source: https://cafe.ch/ (read 2026-10-04); https://www.internetcafe.ch/geschichte/index (search result read 2026-10-04); http://www.biwidus.ch/text/t00/0024.html (search result read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_caf%C3%A9 (read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: The Internet Café at Uraniastrasse 3 in Zurich, as it looked after its renovation in 2006

headline: 1995 in review: shares up 34 percent, the best year of the game so far
text: The S&P 500 rose 34% in 1995 to 615.93, after first closing above 500 on 24 March. The Dow passed 4,000 on 23 February and 5,000 on 21 November and ended the year at 5,117.12, up 33.5%. The economy has absorbed the Fed's rate rises of 1994, and investment in new technology picked up late in the year.
